original_question: On which chromosome is the gene that is associated with Roberts syndrome located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene that is associated with Roberts syndrome located?
final_qi.long_answer: Roberts syndrome is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the ESCO2 gene (Establishment of Sister Chromatid Cohesion N-Acetyltransferase 2). The ESCO2 locus is situated on the short arm of human chromosome 8 (band 8p21.1), so the disease-associated gene resides on chromosome 8.
